comment: Golden vectors for board series ingest validation.
A series' column types are fixed at creation, and every push is
checked against them. That check is the contract between an agent
writing a board and everything that later renders it, so it is
pinned here rather than living only in inline unit tests.
Two rules drive most of these and are easy to regress:
1. NULL IS A GAP, NOT A ZERO. Null is legal in every column. A
board that renders a missing sample as 0 reports an outage
2. MISMATCH IS AN ERROR, NEVER A COERCION. A string '12' in a
number column, or 3.5 in an integer column, fails the push.
Coercing hides a writer bug until the chart is unreadable.

vectors.name: fully populated row
every column accepts null as a gap
a null number is a gap, not zero
negative and zero numbers are ordinary values
integer column accepts a large i64
number column accepts an integer literal
timestamp with a non-UTC offset is accepted and normalized
string column keeps unicode verbatim
string in a number column is not coerced
float in an integer column is not truncated
number in a string column is not stringified
integer 1 is not a bool
bool is not a number
nested object is rejected
array cell is rejected
timestamp without an offset is rejected
date-only timestamp is rejected
epoch seconds are not a timestamp
short row is a column-count mismatch
long row is a column-count mismatch
empty row is a column-count mismatch
